name: Optima Music Reference Library
purpose: Every YouTube video used across the K-12 Optima music courses, with what it is, which course and module uses it, and where it meets the art and ELA libraries.

math.proportion.label: Proportion and ratio
math.proportion.note: Intervals, tuning and time signatures are ratios. The same idea the art library files under canons of proportion.

science.acoustics.label: Acoustics and how sound works
science.acoustics.note: Vibration, overtones and resonance: why an instrument sounds the way it does.

science.anatomy.label: Human anatomy
science.anatomy.note: Breath, embouchure and the body as the instrument.

science.perception.label: Perception and the brain
science.perception.note: How listeners feel a beat and attach emotion to sound.

ela.poetry-set-to-music.label: Poetry set to music
ela.poetry-set-to-music.note: A poem that became a song. Joins the ELA catalogue by author.

ela.narrative-in-music.label: Story told without words
ela.narrative-in-music.note: Programme music: narrative carried by instruments alone.

ela.classical-myth.label: Classical myth
ela.classical-myth.note: Greek and Roman myth as subject matter, shared with the art library.

history.ancient-greece.label: Ancient Greece
history.ancient-greece.note: Greek musical thought, where the Western account of scale and ratio starts.

history.harlem-renaissance.label: The Harlem Renaissance
history.harlem-renaissance.note: Joins the art library's Harlem Renaissance works and the ELA catalogue's Harlem Renaissance writers.

history.civil-rights.label: Civil rights and protest
history.civil-rights.note: Music used as protest and as an anthem.

legacy_note: MI-1, MI-2, MI-3 and one M/J Music Theory 1 section export an IDENTICAL 116-video pool, so a Canvas export cannot say which course teaches a video. Course attribution therefore comes only from the renovated build folders.
scope_note: scope="video" means the video itself is that thing. scope="lesson" means the Optima lesson using it is about that thing. Every tag names the string that justified it.
